newsitem.title: UK: Yeltsin heart operation lifts dollar.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin heart operation lifts dollar.

text.p: News that Boris Yeltsin is to have heart surgery lifted the dollar on an otherwise quiet day in Europe's markets on Thursday which saw shares end with small advances despite a bout of nerves over U.S. jobs data.
The U.S. currency rose to around 1.4850 against the mark on short-covering, touching a high of 1.4856 after being stuck around 1.4815 during the morning.
"The safehaven argument worked again on the Yeltsin news but the impact was fairly limited," Pat Magill at Daiwa Europe said, referring to the dollar.
News that the Russian president is likely to have a heart operation at the end of September in Moscow, sent Russian shares and bonds reeling.
"Everybody is selling and it is not looking good," said Nick Mokhoff, head of Russian equities trading at Alliance-Menatep.

The dollar also firmed back above 109 yen, helped by news of an 81 percent year-on-year fall in Japan's custom-cleared trade surplus in August. But it failed to clear resistance at 109.10 yen amid talk of a large sell order around that level.
Earlier attention had been on the French franc which came under pressure overnight when the mark spiked up to 3.4315 francs overnight, its strongest level since March 22.
Dealers said the French central bank intervened to buy francs at 3.4300 in defence of its franc fort policy.

The franc's dip was prompted by data on Wednesday which showed that France's economy shrank 0.4 percent in the second quarter, then data on Thursday which showed Germany's economy strengthed 1.5 percent over the same period -- beyond most economists' expectations.
But economists said the franc had overreacted because the French and German economic situations were not as different as headline gross domestic product figures suggested.

"When you juxtapose the German and French GDP numbers, people get nervous," Smith Barney economist Steven Englander said. But, he added "the German economy isn't that strong and the French economy isn't that weak."
The franc had regained its poise by late European trade when the mark/franc cross stood had rebounded to 3.4237. Its old Exchange Rate Mechanism floor was 3.4305 per mark.
As expected German and French interest rates were left unchanged by the Bundesbank and the Bank of France which both held routine meetings today.

Europe's leading share markets opened steady to firmer, but tacked back when Wall Street opened slightly weaker after figures released by the U.S. Labour Department showed that new applications for unemployment benefits fell by an unexpectedly sharp 15,000 last week -- after four straight weeks of rises.
The news reinforced fears about Friday's key U.S. jobs report for August -- a significant indicator of the trend in the Federal Reserve's interest rate policy.

At the end of business, London's FTSE-100 Index of leading British shares -- Europe's biggest market -- was up 0.37 percent, while French shares were up 0.58 percent on the back of strong corporate figures -- notably from Danone and Carrefour.
Caution over U.S. jobs and interest rates remained in the key theme, however.
French traders were also waiting for Prime Minister Alain Juppe's tax reform address later in the day.

German shares ended bourse trade a touch lower, but posted a 0.25 percent gain in post-bourse electronic trading. The market shrugged off a small rise in German jobless data for August and the GDP data, though buying interest was limited.
CURRENCIES AT 1530 GMT
The dollar was at 1.4850 marks and 109.10 yen after 1.4815 marks and 108.80 yen late on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS - CLOSING RATES
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares finished up 14.5 points at 3,887.2.
Frankfurt's 30-share DAX index ended bourse trade down 2.85 at 2,529.54. The IBIS DAX later rose to 2,532.55 in computerised business.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index finished up 11.46 at 1,996.23.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $386 an ounce, unchanged from the morning, and closed London business at $386.35 after ending at $385.65 on Wednesday. Silver rose two cents to $5.20.
